value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Arvin/Kern County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: Valid City of Arvin Business License (contractor)
Job card / approved plans on-site at inspection

value: Call Arvin's Building Division at (661) 854-2822 with the permit number ready to schedule inspection
Approved plans, permit, and job card must be present on-site at the time of inspection

value.notes: The City's own SolarAPP+ Permitting page states that once the SolarAPP+ application is submitted and paid for through the City's Permit Portal, 'Your permit will be issued automatically' — i.e. same-day/instant issuance for SolarAPP+-eligible projects.

value.program_or_pathway: SolarAPP+ automated permitting (three-step process: SolarAPP+ submission, Arvin Permit Portal issuance, inspection scheduling)
other_conditions: Contractors must register at gosolarapp.org and pay the SolarAPP+ processing fee before applying through the city's own Permit Portal
Initial SolarAPP+ fee covers up to three revisions
